 PVR INOX (NSE:PVRINOX): What Does Its New Jaipur IMAX Cinema Mean?
 PVRINOX
 Source: Krish Capital Pty Ltd
 You are reading a free article with opinions that may differ from the recommendation given by Kalkine in its paid research reports. Become a Kalkine member today to get access to our research reports, in-depth technical and fundamental research. Learn More 
 PVR INOX Limited (NSE:PVRINOX) filed an exchange announcement on 4 November 2026 disclosing the opening of a new five-screen cinema at Pacific Mall, VT Road, Mansarovar, Jaipur, Rajasthan, bringing its total network to 1,802 screens across 359 properties in 114 cities.
 Key Highlights
 The new Jaipur property at Pacific Mall, Mansarovar features one IMAX auditorium and four premium mainstream auditoriums with a total seating capacity of 949 seats.
 This is Rajasthan's first IMAX screen, taking PVR INOX's nationwide IMAX count to 27 screens across its network.
 The cinema is equipped with 4K laser projection, Dolby Surround Sound, next-generation 3D technology, Celebrity Recliners, and self-ordering food kiosks.
 With this addition, PVR INOX operates 78 screens across eight cinemas in Jaipur, making it the city's largest multiplex operator.
 About the Company
 PVR INOX Limited (NSE:PVRINOX) , headquartered in Gurugram, is India's largest film exhibition company. It was formed through the merger of PVR Limited and INOX Leisure Limited in 2023 and operates 1,802 screens across 359 properties in 114 cities in India and Sri Lanka. Its portfolio includes premium large-format screens, IMAX auditoriums, and curated food and beverage offerings across the Consumer Brands and Retail sector.
 Announcement in Detail
 According to the exchange filing dated 4 November 2026, PVR INOX Limited opened its eighth cinema in Jaipur at Pacific Mall, VT Road, Mansarovar, Rajasthan. The five-screen property has a seating capacity of 949 seats and includes one IMAX auditorium alongside four premium mainstream auditoriums. The cinema features 4K laser projection, Dolby Surround Sound, and next-generation 3D technology. The launch coincided with the festive season and the opening of the film Ramayana, which led the new property's initial screening line-up.
 The new property is situated inside Pacific Mall, Mansarovar, described in the press release as North India's largest mall and Rajasthan's most premium retail and entertainment destination. The addition of the IMAX screen marks the first such format in Rajasthan, lifting PVR INOX's total IMAX screen count nationally to 27. The venue also features Celebrity Recliners and a Cinema Food Court concept with self-ordering kiosks, extending the company's premium hospitality offering alongside its audiovisual technology formats.
 Impact on Investors
 Investors will note that this opening increases PVR INOX's total screen count to 1,802 across 359 properties, expanding the company's footprint in Rajasthan, a geography where it previously had no IMAX presence. The filing shows that the Jaipur network now stands at 78 screens across eight properties, making it one of the larger city-level clusters in the company's portfolio.
 The disclosed terms indicate this is an organic capacity addition rather than an acquisition or financial restructuring, so no dilution to existing shareholders arises from this announcement. Shareholders will observe that the addition of premium formats such as IMAX and 4K laser projection is consistent with the company's stated strategy of introducing differentiated cinema formats in key urban markets, as described in the exchange filing.
 Sector / Market Context
 India's multiplex exhibition sector has seen increasing adoption of premium large formats, with operators investing in IMAX, 4DX, and Dolby Cinema auditoriums to differentiate from home streaming alternatives. According to publicly available data from the Multiplex Association of India, organised multiplex screens in India have grown steadily as operators expand into Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities. Jaipur, as one of Rajasthan's largest urban centres, represents a significant catchment for premium entertainment spending, and the introduction of IMAX into the city reflects broader industry trends toward format-led differentiation rather than purely volume-driven screen expansion.
